topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement and sets expectations regarding its complexity and importance.

topics.label: Complement system overview and core biochemistry
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, naming conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three biochemical cascades through which complement is recognized and deposited onto pathogen surfaces to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream functional outcomes generated once complement activation takes place.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in specific complement proteins lead to distinct clinical disease phenotypes.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens circumvent complement defenses and how these bacterial factors are applied in biotechnology.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion on complement and outlines the subject of the upcoming lecture.
